---
title: "Super Bowl Economics & Game Dynamics"
subtitle: "Trends in advertising costs and scoring patterns across Super Bowls I–LII (1967–2018)"
---

An R / Quarto data analysis examining how the cost of Super Bowl advertising has evolved over five decades, and whether more competitive games tend to be higher scoring.

## Research Questions

1. Is there a relationship between time (year) and the cost of a 30-second Super Bowl advertisement?
2. Is there a relationship between margin of victory and total points scored — do closer games score more?

## Key Findings

- Year vs. ad cost: **R = 0.931, R² = 0.866**. Very strong positive relationship; about 87% of the variation in ad cost is associated with year.
- Margin of victory vs. total points: **R = 0.280, R² = 0.078**. Weak association; competitiveness is not a strong predictor of total points scored.
